reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) does not directly support the key premises. E1 mentions general concepts of intermetallic design and controlled oxide formation in Mg alloys but provides no specific data on metastable solid solutions, precipitation kinetics, or the dual role of precipitates in oxidation/corrosion. E2 discusses microstructural evolution in refractory superalloys (AlMo0.5NbTa0.5TiZr-based, no Mg) and only notes coarsening of Al-Zr intermetallics, without addressing oxide nucleation or corrosion behavior. The premises thus lack specific prior evidence.
premises: Mg-containing HEA can be prepared in a metastable single-phase solid solution state
Diffusion-controlled precipitation of intermetallics occurs during high-temperature exposure
Fine intermetallic precipitates can act as nucleation sites for protective oxide films (TiO2, MgO)
Coarsening and interconnection of precipitates disrupt passivation and promote galvanic corrosion
A transition from protective to deleterious behavior occurs at a critical precipitate size/morphology
